parole.significato: soul (the immaterial, spiritual part of a person, often understood as distinct from the body)

parole.significato: adds emphasis to a statement or а question
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Church Slavonic ѥлѣ (jelě), from Proto-Slavic *je lě.

Inherited from Old Church Slavonic жѩдьнъ (žjędĭnŭ), from Proto-Slavic *žędьnъ.

parole.significato: used to form (periphrastic) future and future perfect tense
parole.testo: Convergence of ща да (šta da, “to will, to seek to”) (< Old Church Slavonic хътѣти (xŭtěti)< Proto-Slavic *xъtěti) and dialectal жъда́ (žădá, “to await”) (< Old Church Slavonic жьдати (žĭdati)< Proto-Slavic *žьdati).

parole.significato: yellowhammer (passarine bird of genus Emberiza citrinella)
parole.testo: Derived from желт (želt). By surface analysis, желт (želt) + -ва (-va). Cognate with Bulgarian же́лва (žélva) and Bulgarian жъ́лва (žắlva) from Etymology 1.

Inherited from Old Church Slavonic жрѣбьць (žrěbĭcĭ), from Proto-Slavic *žerbьcь.

parole.significato: to venerate, to worship, to perform a rite

parole.significato: loan, borrowing (money, goods, or resources given temporarily to someone with the expectation of repayment or return)

parole.significato: play, game (activity for amusement, entertainment, or sport)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Church Slavonic игрь (igrĭ), from Proto-Slavic *jьgra.

parole.significato: to choose, to select, to pick out, to single out

parole.testo: Inherited from Old Church Slavonic колѣбати сѧ (kolěbati sę), from Proto-Slavic *kolěbati sę.
